story.head: Somebody has to win
paras: The Blue Jackets won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-3 in overtime in Philadelphia on Oct 27. The Jackets are on a three-game losing streak, and the Flyers (5-10-6) lost 3-2 in overtime to Edmonton on Wednesday. Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Flyers seventh (tied for 27th in the NHL) and the Blue Jackets last (29th).

The Flyers’ record (.381) is about what their chances are worth. The Blue Jackets have played better than their record (.412) says: their chances are worth about .486, and their finishing has held them back.

The Flyers play slow, tight games (2nd lowest) and get a lot of their shots blocked (31st). They also block a lot of shots (4th), so the Flyers are likely to get in the way of a lot of the Blue Jackets’ shots. Philadelphia has scored 2.24 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. The Blue Jackets forecheck as hard as almost anyone (3rd) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (29th). They also get their defensemen shooting (2nd), so their defensemen shoot a lot, and the Flyers’ not so much. Columbus has scored 2.35 goals a game, the third fewest in the league.

Matvei Michkov (10 G / 5 A / 15 P in 21 GP) leads the Flyers in scoring, and Trevor Zegras (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 21 GP) is next in line. For the Blue Jackets, Kent Johnson (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Zach Werenski (2 G / 12 A / 14 P in 17 GP) is next in line.

Cam Talbot (5-3-0 / .907 SV% in 8 GS) will likely start for Columbus. Philadelphia has two options in net: Dan Vladař (3-4-4 / .879 SV% in 11 GS) and Joseph Woll (2-6-2 / .901 SV% in 10 GS). Vladař has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Wednesday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
